title: HELIX Terminology: Absence Type
description: Categories of employee absence from work with associated leave policies.

codes.definition: Paid time off accrued based on length of service and appointment type. Accrual rates and maximum balances vary by employee class. Faculty on academic-year appointments typically do not accrue vacation.
Paid leave for personal illness, medical appointments, or care of an immediate family member. Many states mandate sick leave accrual. Some institutions have sick leave donation/sharing programs.
Paid leave for personal business not covered by other leave categories. Typically limited to 2-3 days per year. May or may not require advance approval.

Leave protected under the Family and Medical Leave Act. Up to 12 weeks of job-protected, unpaid leave per year for qualifying reasons (serious health condition, new child, military family). Runs concurrent with paid leave if available.

Leave for military service under USERRA (Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act). Job-protected with reemployment rights. Many institutions provide differential pay (difference between military and civilian pay).
Paid leave following the death of a family member. Duration typically varies by relationship (3-5 days for immediate family, 1 day for extended family). Definition of 'family' varies by policy.
Leave for serving on a jury or responding to a subpoena. Most institutions provide paid leave for the duration of service. Employee may be required to submit jury fee to the institution.

Extended leave (typically one semester at full pay or one year at half pay) granted to tenured or senior faculty for research, writing, or professional development. Usually available after 6-7 years of service. Requires application and approval.
Leave for birth, adoption, or foster placement of a child. May be paid or unpaid depending on institutional policy. Increasingly offered as a standalone benefit beyond FMLA. Typically 6-12 weeks.
Paid leave directed by the institution, typically during an investigation, restructuring, or emergency. Not initiated by the employee. May be with or without restrictions on campus access.

Leave due to a work-related injury or illness covered under state workers' compensation law. Benefits include medical treatment and wage replacement (typically 2/3 of average weekly wage, subject to state maximums).

Approved leave without pay when paid leave is exhausted or not applicable. Employment relationship maintained but benefits eligibility may be affected. Often requires VP/provost approval beyond a certain duration.
Leave for attending conferences, workshops, certifications, or training. Usually paid with expenses covered by the department or professional development fund.
